title: New noise by-law adopted; South Fergus plan deferred
subtitle: Water meter vendors, procedure by-law deferral, restrictive covenant removal, and a public meeting on a farm severance rezoning
overview: Council adopted a new township-wide Noise By-law, repealing By-law 5001-05, and passed it into law as By-law 6001-24 {{vote:m5}} {{vote:m9}}. Staff said the by-law was developed with the other Wellington municipalities and the County so that the same wording can be enforced by the OPP. A delegate from Elora had asked for decibel limits, clearer definitions and more public input, and some councillors shared those concerns.

Council deferred two items to a Committee of the Whole meeting to be scheduled in April: the South Fergus Secondary Plan and Master Environmental Servicing Plan {{vote:m4}}, and the draft amendments to the Procedure By-law {{vote:m8}}. A councillor with a conflict of interest on the South Fergus item did not take part in that discussion.

Council also named Neptune Technology Inc. and Evans Supply Corporation as vendors of record for water meter infrastructure {{vote:m6}}. It authorized staff to apply to delete an old restrictive covenant from a Glengarry Crescent property {{vote:m7}}. Consent items covered reports on the Metcalfe Street sewer repair, wastewater performance and the 25th amalgamation anniversary {{vote:m3}}. A public meeting was held on a rezoning for a farm surplus dwelling severance at 8196 Wellington Road 19. The minutes report nothing from the closed session on land.

decisions.detail: Council authorized the Mayor and Clerk to execute a new township-wide Noise By-law and repeal By-law 5001-05 {{vote:m5}}.
By-law 6001-24, regulating and prohibiting noise in the township, was read three times and passed {{vote:m9}}.
Council deferred the South Fergus Secondary Plan (OPA 14) and Master Environmental Servicing Plan to a Committee of the Whole meeting in April {{vote:m4}}.
Council deferred the draft procedural by-law changes to a Committee of the Whole meeting in April {{vote:m8}}.
Council named Neptune Technology Inc. as manufacturer of choice and Evans Supply Corporation as vendor of record for Neptune water meter infrastructure {{vote:m6}}.
Council authorized the Managing Director of Planning and Development to apply to delete restrictive covenants from the title of the Newdon Industries Limited property {{vote:m7}}.
As part of the consent agenda, Council confirmed Norma Seibert as a Tenant Director of the Grand River Non-Profit Housing Board {{vote:m3}}.

debate: A delegate argued the Noise By-law needs tweaking, not a rewrite. The delegate asked for decibel limits and sound guides, clearer definitions, and coverage of patio music, fireworks, busking, vehicle idling and places of worship. The delegate also questioned the lack of public input and called wording such as noise 'likely to disturb' too arbitrary.

Staff said the broad wording gives officers discretion and is legally useful for prosecution. They said it was reviewed by the township's legal counsel and the prosecutor. Staff said decibel limits were avoided because the township lacks the equipment and trained staff, and that all municipalities must adopt identical wording for OPP enforcement. Fireworks and busking fall under other by-laws.

Some councillors worried about the by-law's ambiguity and about competing live music on Elora's narrow streets. Others favoured passing it now and revisiting it as a living document if problems arise. Staff said the by-law is one tool among several, alongside AGCO involvement and business responsibility.

On South Fergus, councillors raised concerns about the safety of crossing Highway 6, the gateway design, and having only two neighbourhood parks for a large population. Some also questioned whether buildings of up to eight storeys suit the area. The consultant said park locations are flexible and the 5% parkland dedication is the legal maximum. Council chose to defer to allow more questions and discussion.

On the Procedure By-law, councillors objected to cutting delegation time from ten minutes to five and to the change to the meeting curfew. They asked for a tracked-changes version showing the reasons for each change. Staff said the five-minute limit mainly helps when there are many delegations and that the chair can extend it.
